text: A simple daily growing degree-day calculation in degrees C days is the greater of zero and the average of daily maximum and minimum Celsius temperatures minus the chosen base temperature. Accumulate daily values only over a declared interval and state the crop or organism-specific base and any method-specific upper or lower temperature caps. The AAFC growing-degree-day service documents the thermal-time concept and a defined growing-season window. A GDD total describes thermal accumulation; by itself it does not predict harvested yield, prove crop stage in a particular field, or establish a management trigger. Source basis: Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada growing-degree-day service description. This is a project-authored method summary, not a forecast.
title: Project synthesis: simple growing degree-day arithmetic

quality.temporal_scope: stable_method_summary; current farm and market inputs required

text: For an explicitly chosen cost boundary, break-even price per harvested unit equals the selected cost per acre divided by expected harvested units per acre; break-even yield equals the selected cost per acre divided by an assumed selling price per unit. Keep the cost boundary visible: operating-cost break-even differs from total-cost break-even that includes land, machinery, labour and other ownership costs. Do not rename a user-supplied total cost as operating cost. Both quantities are scenario calculations, not current cash bids, guaranteed yields or sale recommendations. Check moisture and grade, storage, freight, contracts, crop insurance and current local prices before a business decision. Source basis: a Manitoba Agriculture cost-production guide; dated example crop prices in that guide are deliberately excluded.
title: Project synthesis: crop-budget break-even price and yield

quality.temporal_scope: stable_method_summary; current farm and market inputs required

text: For a crop enterprise budget, construct a price-by-yield sensitivity grid from declared farm input values and calculate net return for each combination. Keep crop year and units explicit. Distinguish variable costs from fixed or shared costs, and do not count machinery ownership twice. A historical cost guide supplies an example budget structure, not a current cash bid, forecast, or farm cost. A cash-flow calendar records when bills and crop-sale receipts occur; it differs from projected accrual net return. Source basis: a provincial special-crop cost guide and USDA ARS WHOLEFARM planning description. This project-authored framework does not prescribe a crop or transaction.
title: Project synthesis: crop-budget price and yield sensitivity

quality.temporal_scope: stable_method_summary; current farm and market inputs required

text: Seed-lot germination and field seedling survival are different measurements. A germination test estimates viable seed under test conditions; losses between germination and an emerged stand depend on soil moisture, temperature, residue, depth, disease, insects and equipment placement. Record the target stand, lot germination, thousand-kernel weight, assumed emergence loss, drill setting, and observed stand after emergence. Recalculate the expected seed mass when those inputs change. If thousand-kernel weight or germination is unknown, a precise purchase quantity cannot be calculated from the target stand alone. Source basis: Manitoba Agriculture, Seeding Rates for Spring Cereals, pages 3-4. No universal mortality percentage or final population is asserted here.
title: Project synthesis: seedling survival is an assumption to verify

quality.temporal_scope: stable_method_summary; current farm and market inputs required

text: For a spring-cereal planning scenario, calculate the expected established-seed fraction as laboratory germination fraction times one minus the anticipated post-germination seedling-loss fraction. The thousand-kernel-weight method estimates seed mass in lb/ac as target plants per square foot multiplied by thousand-kernel weight in grams, divided by ten times the expected established-seed fraction. This estimates seed to place, not a guaranteed final stand. Check the actual lot weight and germination, locally appropriate target stand, seedbed and emergence history, then calibrate the drill and count emergence. Source basis: a provincial spring-cereal seeding-rate guide. This project-authored formula summary supplies neither a cultivar target nor a field recommendation.
title: Project synthesis: spring-cereal seeding-rate calculation

quality.temporal_scope: stable_method_summary; current farm and market inputs required

text: A balance-sheet current ratio is current farm assets divided by current farm liabilities. Debt-to-asset ratio is farm debt divided by farm assets; multiply the fraction by one hundred to express a percentage. The first is a liquidity measure and the second a solvency measure. Neither one number alone establishes profitability, repayment capacity or whether a particular investment is wise. Keep statement date, asset valuation, farm-versus-household boundary and ratio definition consistent when comparing years or operations. USDA ERS publishes sector-level ratio definitions, which are not a diagnosis of an individual farm. Source basis: USDA Economic Research Service, Documentation for the Farm Sector Financial Ratios; this is a project-authored arithmetic summary.
title: Project synthesis: farm liquidity and solvency ratios

quality.temporal_scope: stable_method_summary; current farm and market inputs required

text: A crop nutrient plan reconciles a realistic crop yield goal and nutrient demand with soil and plant test information, available nutrients in manure or other amendments, previous-crop credits, expected availability and loss pathways. Then consider nutrient source, rate, timing and placement for the specific crop, soil, season and field. Test a changed manure or amendment source before assuming its nutrient content. A mapped soil class or generic soil-health description is regional context and cannot by itself calculate a field fertilizer rate. Use locally calibrated guidance, current rules and representative field samples for any prescription; U.S. NRCS planning concepts cannot establish Canadian fertilizer law or a Saskatchewan canola rate. Source basis: USDA NRCS Nutrient Management; this is a project-authored planning summary.
title: Project synthesis: nutrient planning inputs and authority boundary

publisher: Iowa State University Extension and Outreach

text: For an incremental farm decision, compare only cash and noncash items that change. Net change per acre or per farm equals added revenue plus saved costs minus added costs minus lost revenue, all on the same time and acreage basis. Include unpaid labour, machinery ownership, depreciation and timing when they truly change, and distinguish a one-time purchase from annual costs. The result is conditional on yield, price, labour and operating assumptions; compare optimistic and adverse scenarios instead of treating a positive estimate as guaranteed profit. Source basis: Iowa State University Extension Ag Decision Maker, Partial Budgeting: A Tool to Analyze Farm Business Changes, updated October 2024. This is a project-authored method summary, not copied source text.
title: Project synthesis: four-part partial budget for a farm change

quality.temporal_scope: stable_method_summary; current farm and market inputs required

text: A crop enterprise budget estimates revenue and costs for a crop and acreage under declared yield, price and cost assumptions. A whole-farm plan also combines enterprises, rotation and acreage constraints, machinery ownership, land arrangements, financing and a month-by-month cash-flow schedule. Positive expected net return for one crop does not ensure enough cash is available when seed, rent, payroll, debt service or other bills fall due. Keep cash receipts/payments distinct from accrual profit, inventory value and noncash depreciation, and test lower-yield or delayed-sale scenarios. Source basis: USDA ARS National Peanut Research Laboratory's WHOLEFARM planning description; this is a project-authored conceptual summary, not an assertion that its software or old budget figures are currently applicable.
title: Project synthesis: enterprise return and whole-farm cash flow
